channel.project_pack_ref: Hybrid First-Year Teaching Redesign with Virtual Learning Environments

threads.thread_goal: Align on overall hybrid course structure and weekly plan.

messages.text: Hi team, I've put together a first draft of the new course structure. Please see the 'Hybrid Course Outline and Weekly Plan' (A1). The goal is to get T1 completed this week. Let me know your thoughts on the flow and the balance of on-site vs. online sessions.

Thanks for getting this started. I've had a look at A1. The overall structure seems solid, but I'm wondering if Week 3's topic should be swapped with Week 4's. Introducing the core theoretical model before the practical application in Week 4 might provide better scaffolding for the students.
I agree with that suggestion. It also means the lab session in Week 4 would align directly with the new topic, which makes more sense. That lab definitely needs to be on-site.

Good point on the scaffolding. I also noticed one of the learning outcomes for Week 2 seems a bit ambitious. Could we break it down and spread it across Week 2 and 3? It might help students who need more time to process complex ideas.
All excellent feedback. So, the proposal is: 1. Swap topics for Week 3 and 4. 2. Refine the Week 2 learning outcome, splitting it across two weeks. This seems much stronger.

Based on that, here's a proposed online/on-site split for the first four weeks:
Week 1: Intro (On-site)
Week 2: Foundational Concepts (Online async)
Week 3: Application Case Studies (Online sync)
Week 4: Core Theory & Lab (On-site)

Does this work for everyone?
Works for me. That's a good mix.
Yes, that looks logical.
Sorry for the delay. I've just caught up on the thread. The proposed changes to A1 and the weekly delivery modes look good to me.

Great, thanks for confirming everyone. We have a decision. The weekly structure and learning outcomes are approved with the adjustments (D1), and we've agreed on the online vs on-site delivery for the first four weeks (D2). I'll update A1 to reflect this now.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize assessment plan, rubrics, and feedback approach.

messages.text: Afternoon all. I've drafted the 'Assessment Map and Rubrics Register' (A2) for our review, which covers T2. I've aimed for a balance of formative and summative tasks, but I'd appreciate your eyes on the weightings and deadlines.

Thanks for this. The summative tasks look good. I'm wondering if we could add one more low-stakes formative task in Week 3? Just a quick check for understanding before they hit the first major assignment in Week 5. It could be a simple peer-review activity.

I like the peer-review idea. Looking at the deadlines in A2, the presentation in Week 7 and the lab report in Week 8 are very close together. That could create a bottleneck for students and for our marking. Could we move the report deadline to Week 9?
Good catch. Moving the lab report to Week 9 is a sensible adjustment. I support adding the formative peer-review task as well; it's a good way to build their feedback skills.

Great suggestions. I'll add the peer-review task and shift the report deadline. That brings us to feedback consistency. To support T10, I suggest we all contribute to a shared comment bank. It would help align our feedback, especially on the rubrics. This is also mentioned in the 'Teaching Team Communication and Feedback Norms' (A6).

A comment bank is a great idea. To make it effective, maybe we should have a short 30-minute calibration meeting before the first assignment is due, just to make sure we're all interpreting the rubric criteria in the same way.
A calibration session is a must. It will save us a lot of trouble later. I can help set that up.

Perfect. Let's lock these decisions in. We confirm the assessment types, weightings, and deadlines with the proposed adjustments (D3). And we agree to use a shared comment bank for T10 and hold a calibration session to ensure shared feedback standards (D4). I will update A2 accordingly.

threads.thread_goal: Define inclusion strategies and support for learning difficulties.

messages.text: Hi everyone, as part of T5, I've drafted an 'Inclusion and Learning Difficulties Support Guide' (A3). It contains a range of potential adjustments. I'd like us to agree on a few core practices that we will all apply consistently. Please share your thoughts.

Thanks for drafting this. I think providing lecture notes and slides at least 24 hours in advance should be a baseline requirement for all of us, not just an adjustment. It's a simple thing that has a huge impact for many students.

I strongly agree with the advance notes. I'd also add that for any group work, we should provide suggested roles or a simple structure. This can really help students who struggle with executive function to engage with the task rather than getting lost in the group's organisation.
Both are excellent, practical suggestions. Are they feasible for everyone to implement every week? Just want to ensure we can commit to what we agree on.

I think they are. The advance notes just requires a bit of planning, and the group roles can be a simple template. I'd also propose a third core practice: running all documents we upload through the VLE's built-in accessibility checker.

That's a great list. So, to formalise the decision (D5), our core adjustments will be: 1. Materials provided 24hrs in advance. 2. Structured roles for group work. 3. Mandatory use of the VLE accessibility checker. Does everyone agree?
Agreed.
Yes, sounds good.
Excellent. I'll update A3 with these as our core practices. I'll also start drafting the plan for the student check-ins mentioned in T11.

threads.thread_goal: Lock down VLE configuration, orientation module, and tracking processes.

messages.text: Hi team, quick update on T4. I've configured the main VLE course shell according to the 'VLE Course Shell Configuration Checklist' (A4). Placeholders for the first four weeks are in place. Could you take a quick look and let me know if the navigation feels intuitive?
Looks great, very clean and easy to follow. I've already started uploading the first set of digital materials for week 1 (T3).

This is looking good. A question about the student orientation module (T9). Where will that live? I think it should be easily accessible, not buried in Week 1. Maybe a 'Start Here' section at the very top?
Yes, my plan was to put it in a permanent announcement block at the top of the course page so it's always visible. I'll get that set up based on the overview in A7.

A permanent block is the right approach. Now, regarding T8, how should we manage attendance and participation tracking? The template in A8 is fine for on-site sessions, but what's our method for tracking engagement with the online materials?
We could use the VLE's activity completion report, maybe tied to viewing a resource or posting in a forum. It's not perfect but it's a simple proxy.

The problem with forum posts is that it can encourage quantity over quality. What if we use a very short, non-graded weekly quiz on the key concept from the async material? It's a more meaningful check of engagement and easy to track automatically in the VLE.
I like the quiz idea. It's a clear, consistent metric. We can set it up to be automated.

Okay, let's make a decision. We approve the VLE structure with the orientation module in a permanent top block (D6). For tracking, we'll use the VLE tool for synchronous sessions and a weekly low-stakes quiz for asynchronous participation (D7).
Sounds good. I'll finalize the VLE shell and set up the orientation module (T9).
And I'll take on defining the process for the tracking and setting up the first quiz template (T8).

threads.thread_goal: Align on hybrid lab/practical procedures and team operations guide.

messages.text: Hi all, for our final major alignment, I've compiled the 'Teaching Team Operations Guide' (T12). This document consolidates everything, including the draft 'Hybrid Lab and Practical Session Procedures' (A5) and our agreed 'Communication and Feedback Norms' (A6). Please review for final sign-off.

Thanks for pulling this together. I've reviewed the lab procedures in A5. It covers on-site safety well, but what about any practical components students might do remotely? We should probably include a simple risk assessment checklist for them to complete for any at-home work.

That's a critical point. On a related note, for hybrid labs where some students are on-site and some are remote, how do we ensure the remote students are properly included? I suggest a 'remote buddy' system, where an on-site student is paired with a remote one to be their hands and eyes.

Both are excellent additions. A remote risk assessment is essential, and the 'remote buddy' idea is a great way to handle inclusion. I'll add both to the procedures in A5. Thanks for spotting those gaps.
I've reviewed the sections on communication norms (A6) and our feedback turnaround times (T7). They accurately reflect our earlier discussion. Looks good to me.
Just read through the consolidated guide. It looks comprehensive. The additions for the lab procedures sound right.

Great. So, with the inclusion of the remote safety checklist and the remote buddy system in the lab procedures, are we all ready to sign off on the lab procedures and the consolidated teaching operations guide (D8)?
Yes, happy to sign off.
Signed off from me.

Excellent, that's everyone. Decision D8 is confirmed. I will make those final edits to the guide now and circulate the final version for our records, which completes T6 and T12. We're in great shape for the semester start!
